extracted.intended_audience: business owners, marketers, and communications/public-relations professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for how brands should prepare for, respond to, and recover from public relations crises, illustrated with major case studies and best-practice recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate openly with the public and the media to show the company is taking the situation seriously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Johnson & Johnson's immediate, open communication during the Tylenol crisis. Maintain transparency about what happened, what is being done, and known facts; avoid defensive or evasive language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement Tangible Safety or Corrective Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Take concrete actions to address the root cause and prevent recurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Johnson & Johnson introduced tamper-proof packaging after the Tylenol crisis. Corrective actions should be visible, industry-leading where appropriate, and communicated to consumers as part of rebuilding trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis Response Training for Employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide staff with training to prepare for and respond to potential crises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Starbucks closed 8,000 stores for racial-bias training. Regular training ensures employees understand protocols and how to represent the brand during incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Apology and Commitment to Initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue a sincere public apology and commit to substantive initiatives addressing the harm or issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Starbucks’ CEO publicly apologized and committed to broader diversity and inclusion efforts. Apologies should be paired with concrete follow-up actions to restore credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely, Empathetic Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond quickly and with empathy; avoid delayed or non-empathic defenses that can fuel outrage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: United Airlines' initial defensive response escalated backlash; later apology and policy changes were needed. Messaging should acknowledge harm, express empathy, and explain next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy Changes and Operational Reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce policy changes and operational reforms after a crisis to address failures and reduce future risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: United introduced new customer-service-focused policies after the passenger removal incident. Reforms should be specific, implemented promptly, and reported publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop Clear Crisis Protocols (roles and procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish documented crisis management protocols that define roles, responsibilities, and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The blog recommends establishing clear crisis management protocols so every team member understands their role during a crisis; protocols should cover escalation, approvals, and communication channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assemble a Crisis Management Team
rubrics_metrics.description: Form a designated team responsible for executing the crisis protocols and coordinating response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preparation guidance: assemble a crisis management team and ensure it has clear authority, points of contact, and decision-making processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular Training and Simulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct periodic simulations and drills to rehearse crisis scenarios and test protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular training and simulations help teams prepare for potential scenarios; they should be realistic and followed by debriefs to improve plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear Communication: speed, transparency, and empathy
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize speed, transparency, and empathy in all crisis messaging and provide regular updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post emphasizes communicating updates regularly to maintain public trust. Messages should be prompt, candid about knowns/unknowns, and express concern for affected parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-Crisis Review and Lessons Learned
rubrics_metrics.description: After the crisis, perform a thorough review to identify root causes and update policies and plans accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct a post-crisis review to identify lessons learned and prevent recurrence; this is part of the 'Recovery' step and should feed into updated training and protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Media Monitoring System
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish systems to monitor social media and public mentions to detect and track crises in real time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actionable checklist: establish a social media monitoring system to track mentions of your brand; use it to surface issues early and inform response strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive Engagement on Digital Platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use digital communication tools and proactively engage on social media to disseminate information and mitigate backlash.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trend guidance: embrace digital tools for rapid dissemination and active engagement. Proactive engagement can shape narratives before misinformation spreads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create and Regularly Update a Crisis Communication Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a living crisis communication plan that is reviewed and updated regularly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist guidance: create and regularly update a crisis communication plan as part of preparation; ensure contact lists, templates, and escalation paths are current.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership Accountability and Visible Executive Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure senior leadership visibly takes responsibility when appropriate and leads the response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the post show CEO apologies and visible commitments matter; leadership should be prepared to speak, apologize, and outline corrective steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Considerations and Accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Uphold ethical standards and accountability as core principles during crisis response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PRSA is cited emphasizing ethics and accountability; responses should avoid spin and prioritize doing the right thing for stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Outcome Metrics to Evaluate Response Effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure recovery speed, customer sentiment, and commercial indicators to evaluate crisis management success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence cited: companies known for good crisis management recover 10–20% faster; analyze customer sentiment pre/post-crisis and metrics like repurchase intent (e.g., '80% of consumers reported they'd purchase J&J post-crisis'). Use these metrics to assess and improve responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow a Preparation → Response → Recovery Framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach crises in three stages: prepare (planning/training), respond (transparent engagement), and recover (learn and adapt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post outlines steps to take during a crisis: Preparation (team and protocols), Response (transparent updates), Recovery (lessons learned and policy adaptation). Use this lifecycle to structure activities and reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain Regular Communication Cadence During a Crisis
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide regular updates rather than infrequent, ad-hoc statements to sustain public trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit guidance: communicate updates regularly to maintain public trust. Consider scheduled briefings, social updates, and follow-up statements as facts evolve.
